title: Stochastic convex Lipschitz minimization: directional moment bounds and a composite objective; high-probability risk; stochastic full subgradients
summary: Fixed-budget high-probability objective risk under separate norm and directional heavy-tail moments. Source-scoped all-budget envelopes are recorded for an explicitly fixed query-dependent fresh kernel. High-dimensional saturation and statistical regimes match; finite-budget transients remain quantified, and no matching source lower is imported below its dimension or outside its confidence window.

description_paragraphs: Find an approximate global minimizer, with accuracy measured by suboptimality of the complete objective.
$$\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}F(x)$$
The complete objective is $F=f+h$. The properties and information interfaces of the two terms are specified separately.

The objective is $f+h$. The function $f$ is convex and $L$-Lipschitz; $h$ is public, proximable, and $\mu$-strongly convex, with $\mu=0$ allowed. A minimizer lies within distance $R$ of $x_0$. The centered noise norm has $\alpha$th moment at most $\sigma^\alpha$, and every unit-direction projection has $\alpha$th moment at most $\sigma_{\mathrm{dir}}^\alpha$.

Unless another geometry is specified, vectors use the Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$, and matrices and higher derivatives use the corresponding operator norm. The assumptions hold uniformly throughout the declared domain.

Write $F=f+h$ and $F^\star=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^d}F(x)$. The public proximal term $h$ is $\mu$-strongly convex; when $\mu=0$, only convexity is required. The directional centered-moment condition is $\mathbb E_t|\langle u,G_t-\mathbb E_tG_t\rangle|^\alpha\le\sigma_{\mathrm{dir}}^\alpha$ for every unit vector $u$.

Admissible parameter domain:

$$d\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1},\quad L,R>0,\quad\mu\ge0,\quad0<\sigma_{\rm dir}\le\sigma,\quad1<\alpha\le2,\quad0<\delta<1/2,\quad T\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}$$

The public proximal term is proper, closed and convex, and its exact proximal map is available for every positive proximal parameter. It is part of the admissible instance class; the minimax lower bound is not asserted for every arbitrarily prescribed fixed nonquadratic regularizer.

oracle.coupling: The instance fixes a query-dependent response kernel K_x before interaction. Given the query x_t, each raw response is a fresh draw from K_{x_t}, independent of the preceding history and private randomness conditional on x_t. Repeated calls at a frozen query are independent copies of the same kernel. Its mean belongs to the subdifferential of f at that query, and both centered moment bounds hold uniformly over queries. Samples cannot be reused across points. A raw response discarded by rejection or used in a batch still costs one call.
auxiliary_interfaces: The exact proximal map of the public function $h$ is available at zero query cost.

Public upper bounds: $L,\ R,\ \sigma,\ \sigma_{\rm dir}$.
Public lower bounds: $\mu$.
The unknown object is the objective $f$. Access to the composite term $h$, including public information and proximal operations, is specified by the interface below.
Query points lie in $\mathbb{R}^d$; feedback consists of stochastic full subgradients:
$$G_t,\quad \mathbb{E}_tG_t\in\partial f(x_t),\quad\mathbb{E}_t\|G_t-\mathbb{E}_tG_t\|^\alpha\le\sigma^\alpha$$

The instance fixes a query-dependent response kernel K_x before interaction. Given the query x_t, each raw response is a fresh draw from K_{x_t}, independent of the preceding history and private randomness conditional on x_t. Repeated calls at a frozen query are independent copies of the same kernel. Its mean belongs to the subdifferential of f at that query, and both centered moment bounds hold uniformly over queries. Samples cannot be reused across points. A raw response discarded by rejection or used in a batch still costs one call.
The exact proximal map of the public function $h$ is available at zero query cost.
The fixed-kernel interpretation is made explicit for source compatibility. No equivalence to the broader class of history-dependent response kernels is asserted.

output.certificate: No additional certificate is required, although a method may use one internally to select its output.
description_paragraphs: Return a point $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$.
The output may be unqueried or constructed from the query history, provided it is feasible. No additional function value or accuracy certificate is required.
$$\ell(I,x)=F(x)-F^\star,\qquad F=f+h$$
$F^\star=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}F(x)$. The existence, compactness, or initial-suboptimality assumptions ensure that the optimal value in this comparison is finite.

resource.unit_cost: One full stochastic-gradient sample costs one call; a batch of $b$ samples costs $b$ calls.

description_paragraphs: One full stochastic-gradient sample costs one call; a batch of $b$ samples costs $b$ calls.
Cost is bounded uniformly on every execution path. All calls used for initialization, repetition, batching, or candidate verification are counted.

Real arithmetic, precision, and storage applied to already available information are uncharged. Public geometric operations are limited to those explicitly granted by the oracle. Query complexity alone does not imply arithmetic, memory, or communication complexity.

Every raw oracle draw is counted, including rejected observations. The source algorithm may use unrestricted internal computation; no polynomial arithmetic or storage bound follows from the oracle bound.
Private randomization is allowed. Queries, stopping decisions, and postprocessing may adapt to observed feedback.
No additional span, zero-respecting, linear-iteration, or memory restriction is imposed.

Interaction is adaptive to the feedback history. Every actual response is charged separately, including responses in parallel or batch queries. Internal real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged.

guarantees.uniformity: There exists a single algorithm whose guarantee holds uniformly for every admissible instance and response rule. The guarantee is not averaged over an input distribution.
description_paragraphs: Select an algorithm using the public parameters, and then require the following for every admissible instance and response rule:
$$\mathcal{R}_{T,\delta}=\inf_{A:N_A\le T}\inf\{r\ge0:\sup_{I,\mathcal{O}}\Pr(\ell(I,A^{\mathcal{O}})>r)\le\delta\}$$
The probability space includes observation noise and the algorithm's private randomness. The instance and its admissible oracle law are fixed before randomness is averaged.

The budget-to-risk curve is $\mathcal R_{T,\delta}=\inf_{A:N_A\le T}\inf\{r\ge0:\sup_{I,\mathcal O}\Pr(\ell(I,A^{\mathcal O})>r)\le\delta\}$. The budget $T$ is fixed, and the comparison concerns high-probability error. A risk rate is not a query-complexity rate.

symbols.definition: $$\mathcal H_{\mu,R}(z)=\max_{0\le r\le R}(zr-\mu r^2/2)=\begin{cases}Rz,&\mu=0,\\z^2/(2\mu),&\mu>0,\ z\le\mu R,\\Rz-\mu R^2/2,&\mu>0,\ z\ge\mu R.\end{cases}$$

quantities.definition_note: Fixed-budget high-probability risk: the smallest loss threshold whose failure probability is at most delta uniformly over admissible instances and the fixed query-dependent kernels. The probability includes private and oracle randomness. The budget is an almost-sure cap on raw calls. This quantity is not expected loss.

proofs.title: Source-to-target class and symbol map
proofs.body: Set source X=R^d and source r=h, and rename (G,D,L,s,p) as (L,R,sigma,sigma_dir,alpha). The target f is globally Lipschitz on this X, and the target exact prox is exactly the source auxiliary interface. The explicitly fixed query-dependent kernels coincide with the source oracle. Both quantities minimize a uniform failure-probability threshold under an almost-sure raw-call cap. Thus the source upper theorem applies to every target instance. For the lower direction, source Theorem 2.2 uses X=R^d and h(x)=mu*||x||^2/2, including h=0 at mu=0. The source hard functions are globally convex and Lipschitz and obey the same initial-distance and moment budgets; hence they lie in the target class. This argument imports the cited theorem statement, not a reproof of it. To meet the Atlas cap on every execution path, stop before any (T+1)st call and return the last feasible point (or the public initial point). The source already uses at most T calls almost surely on every legal instance, so this change affects only a null event per instance and leaves its success probability unchanged. It does not cover history-adaptive response kernels or claim a lower bound for each individually prescribed public regularizer.

proofs.title: Envelope comparison, sharp subregions and exhaustive row routing
proofs.body: Write H(z)=max_{0<=r<=R}(zr-mu*r^2/2). Maximizing the concave quadratic gives the displayed three branches. H is increasing. For k>=1, H(kz)<=k^2 H(z): substituting r=k*s and enlarging the allowed interval bounds the maximization by k^2 times H(z); the reverse scaling inequality for 0<=k<=1 follows by restricting to r=k*s. If w>=L, both source envelopes are H(L). If a<=C0*w, min(L,v)<= (1+C0)*min(L,w), so the ratio of source envelopes is at most (1+C0)^2. At mu=0 this gives R*w in the nonsaturated region. At mu>0, w<=mu*R gives w^2/(2*mu), and w>mu*R gives R*w-mu*R^2/2. The pure heavy-tail rows use Theorem 2.1 with its complete domination predicate and u<=L (implied by w<L). Their strong row also retains u<=mu*R. The other statistical rows explicitly exclude the pure-heavy rows. A pure-heavy predicate implies a<=C0*w, so it cannot intersect the remaining row a>C0*w. Confidence and dimension are split first, then w>=L versus w<L, then the stated curvature and domination predicates. These nine active rows partition the original native parameter domain for each fixed C0>0. They say nothing about an independent proof verification of the source theorem.

proofs.title: Upper transfer to the remaining native confidence range
proofs.body: For 1/10<=delta<1/2, run the source upper algorithm with delta0=1/20. Its failure probability is at most delta0<=delta and its raw-call cap is still T. Substituting ell0=log(3/delta0)=log(60) into the upper amplitude gives v0 and proves the recorded upper bound in all finite dimensions. A lower bound for the stricter delta0 guarantee would not imply a lower bound for the weaker target delta, so none is imported.
